meta.title: eBay Fee Calculator & 2026 Fee Guide | Checkila
meta.description: See how much eBay actually takes in fees. Current final value fee rates by category and Store tier, the fee formula, and a full FAQ, from Checkila.

hero.h1: eBay Fee Calculator & Complete 2026 Fee Guide
hero.subhead: How much does eBay take in fees? Here's the current rate structure, the formula behind it, and answers to the questions sellers ask most.

ebayFeeCalculator.intro: Every eBay sale involves more than one fee: a final value fee on the sale, a small per-order fee, insertion fees if you're outside your free listing allowance, and optional costs like promoted listings or payment processing. This page breaks down exactly how those fees are calculated in 2026, by category and Store subscription level, so you can price with confidence. To calculate your exact numbers for a specific listing, use the calculator inside your Checkila dashboard.

feeTypes.name: Final value fee (FVF)
feeTypes.what: The main marketplace commission charged when an item sells.
feeTypes.how: A percentage of the total sale (item price + shipping + tax where applicable), plus a small fixed per-order fee.

feeTypes.name: Per-order fee
feeTypes.what: A flat fee applied once per checkout, not per item.
feeTypes.how: Typically $0.30 for orders of $10 or less, and $0.40 for orders above $10.

feeTypes.name: Insertion fee
feeTypes.what: Charged when you create a listing after your free monthly allowance is used.
feeTypes.how: A flat fee per listing that varies by category and Store subscription level.

feeTypes.name: Promoted Listings fee
feeTypes.what: Advertising cost for boosting a listing's visibility.
feeTypes.how: Usually a percentage of the sale price, charged only when a promoted listing actually sells.

feeTypes.name: Payment processing fee
feeTypes.what: Cost of handling the buyer's payment through eBay's managed payments.
feeTypes.how: A percentage of the payout plus a small fixed amount, varying by country.

feeTypes.name: International fee
feeTypes.what: Applies to cross-border sales or currency conversion.
feeTypes.how: A percentage of the sale added when shipping internationally or converting currency.

feeTypes.name: Store subscription fee
feeTypes.what: Monthly or annual cost of an eBay Store plan.
feeTypes.how: A fixed price by tier (Starter, Basic, Premium, Anchor, Enterprise) that unlocks larger free listing allowances and lower fee tiers.

storeTiers.typicalFvf: Often 12.7% up to $2,500, lower in specific categories

formula.label: Total Sale
formula.formula: Item price + buyer-paid shipping + sales tax
formula.explanation: This is the base amount eBay applies most fee percentages to.

formula.label: Final Value Fee
formula.formula: Total Sale × FVF rate + per-order fixed fee
formula.explanation: eBay's core commission on the sale.

formula.label: Promotion Fee
formula.explanation: Only charged when a promoted listing sells.

formula.label: Net Profit
formula.formula: Total Sale − Total Fees − Shipping Cost − Item Cost
formula.explanation: What you actually keep after every fee and cost is accounted for.

glossary.definition: The commission eBay charges when an item sells, as a percentage of the total sale plus a small per-order fee.
A fee for creating a listing once your free monthly allowance is used.
A flat fee applied once per checkout, regardless of how many items are in the order.
A monthly or annual plan that gives larger free listing allowances and often lower final value fees.
The monthly allotment of listings that don't incur an insertion fee.
The minimum price needed to cover all fees and costs, leaving zero profit.
What's left after subtracting all fees, shipping cost and item cost from the sale price.

faq.q: How much does eBay take in fees?
faq.a: It depends on your category, Store subscription and price. eBay charges a final value fee (commonly in the 9-15% range) plus a small per-order fee, and may add insertion, promotion or international fees on top.

faq.q: How are eBay fees calculated?
faq.a: Fees are calculated on the Total Sale — item price plus shipping and tax where applicable. The final value fee applies to that base, and other charges like promotion or insertion fees are added separately.

faq.q: What percentage does eBay take?
faq.a: Percentages vary by category and Store tier, commonly landing around 9-15% for the final value fee, with lower bands on higher-value portions of a sale in many categories.

faq.q: Does eBay charge a fee if an item doesn't sell?
faq.a: Insertion fees apply when you create a listing and are generally non-refundable even if the item doesn't sell, once your free monthly allowance is used.

faq.q: How do I avoid unnecessary eBay fees?
faq.a: Choose the right category and listing format, use your free monthly listing allowance or a Store subscription, and keep promoted listing spend intentional rather than blanket-applied.

faq.q: Is it worth paying for an eBay Store subscription?
faq.a: Often yes for higher-volume sellers — Stores unlock larger free listing allowances and lower fee tiers in many categories. Lower-volume sellers should compare the monthly cost against what they'd actually save.

faq.q: Do I still need to worry about PayPal fees?
faq.a: Mostly no. eBay's managed payments now handle checkout for most sellers, so PayPal is no longer the default payout method.

faq.q: What is a good profit margin on eBay in 2026?
faq.a: Many sellers target a net margin in the low-to-mid teens after all fees, shipping and cost of goods; anything that comfortably clears your costs while leaving room to reinvest is a healthy target.
